rationale: A `PUBLIC` identifier is not a file, and the analyzer published one as an `imports` target. `extractExternalId` read `findDirectChild(externalId, "SystemLiteral") ?? findDirectChild(externalId, "PubidLiteral")` and its notation caller reached further still — `findDirectChild(node, "ExternalID") || (isNotation ? findDirectChild(node, "PublicID") : null)` — so `<!NOTATION GIF PUBLIC "GIF">`, whose grammar shape is a `PublicID` node carrying a `PubidLiteral` and no system literal at all, produced the edge `GIF -imports-> GIF` at `confidence: 1` on a tier table that maps `notation_external_id` to `import_based`. Found as the ONLY `imports` edge in 11,552 corpus files with no site on the parse tree (`containment-ledger.mts` §`imports` site ledger), which is what an invented edge looks like from outside, and then confirmed by two independent counts in `public-id-census.mts`: 299 `ExternalID`/`PublicID` nodes of which 298 carry a `SystemLiteral` and 1 does not, against 469 `imports` edges of which 298 carry `externalIdKind: "system"` and 1 carries `"public"` — the same edge. The two counts agreeing to the edge is what makes the fix scoped rather than guessed. This is the class the powerShell round removed from `New-Object $type`: a value that is not a file published as an edge target. `gif` is the notation under test and `jpeg` is the CONTROL — a notation whose ExternalID does carry a system literal, so a fixture that passed by refusing every notation import would fail here. `pairs` is a second control with the `PUBLIC "pubid" SYSTEM "system-literal"` shape, which XML allows and which must still import the SYSTEM value and never the public one. `plain` is a third control on a general entity. `graphic` is an unparsed entity pointing at the public-id notation by NDATA, which is a `contains` claim and not an import, so the fixture also pins that it did not become one.

forbidRelationships.note: THE FIX. `<!NOTATION gif PUBLIC "GIF">` names no file, so there is no import of any target from `gif`. Constrained on `from` alone rather than on `from`+`target` on purpose: the original defect was the target `GIF`, and a forbid row naming that target would be satisfied by an analyzer that invented a DIFFERENT one instead.
`PUBLIC "pubid" SYSTEM "sys"` carries two literals and only the system one is a path; the public one must never become a target.
`NDATA gif` is a reference to a notation, published as `contains`. It is not an import of the notation's public identifier, and conflating the two is the same defect one level down.

forbidImports.note: the public identifier is not a path and must not appear in `imports` at all
